newsitem.title: FRANCE: INTERVIEW - Moulinex sees no Europe spending rebound.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Moulinex sees no Europe spending rebound.

text.p: Moulinex chairman Pierre Blayau said on Wednesday there were no signs of real recovery in consumer spending in France or in western Europe overall.
"In Europe ... we can't really say that there's been a spectacular recovery in spending," Blayau said in an interview with Reuters.

"The climate in France remains grim, and in the small appliance industry we can't escape that," he said. He said any measures by the new Socialist-led government to stimulate consumption "would be excellent for us".
"The North American market is pulling up sales," he said. He said the dollar's recent strength was modestly beneficial as about 10 percent of Moulinex's turnover is dollar-denominated.

Blayau said some improvement in sales had been seen in Germany in May and June, the British market remained firm, and Italy and Spain looked "middling". Activity in Russia was experiencing a lull, which he said he expects will be temporary.
